ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory AML/KYC screening of all direct and indirect UBOs, directors, officers, and foundation council members against the OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, European Union terrorist list, and Panama's official sanctions-relevant lists. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) must be identified through a risk-based questionnaire and enhanced due diligence, covering family members and close associates, with supporting source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation. The screening must be completed before commencement of name reservation or registration, and any positive hit must be escalated to the Registry and the Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) as applicable under Ley No. 23 de 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicios en Línea (RPP Online)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be written in the Latin alphabet; Spanish is the formal procedural language of the Public Registry. Non-Spanish names may be accepted if transliterated into Latin characters and if the name is clearly distinguishable from all prior registrations. The name must include the expression 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or an unmistakable abbreviation, and may not misrepresent a public-interest foundation, commercial company, trust, or regulated financial institution.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its registered agent shall submit a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración' to the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days of notification, attaching a certified copy of the rejection certificate and an amended name proposal with legal argument. If the reconsideration is dismissed, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Apelación' within 5 business days thereafter, which will be decided by the higher administrative authority. If the administrative appeal is exhausted, the ultimate judicial remedy is a contentious-administrative action before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia, filed within 30 business days of final administrative notice.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_reservation_fee_sop: The 30-day name reservation window may be extended once for an additional 30 days by paying the relevant extension fee through the registered agent and filing an extension request with the Public Registry before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office. A Panama Private Interest Foundation must maintain a physical registered office in Panama at the office of its licensed registered agent. The registered agent must be an attorney or law firm authorized to practice in Panama. For the declared online retail of oversized furniture and home decor, the operational headquarters may remain abroad, but the foundation's registered office and agent address must remain a physical Panama location and such address will be stated in the foundation charter.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a Low_Risk_Standard e-commerce activity with no regulated financial services, the quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection by the Registro Público or the AML/CFT supervisory authority is estimated at approximately 3%–5% in the first year. The risk may rise to more than 10% if adverse media, PEP flag, or sanctions screening hits arise, or if the foundation is selected by the UAF for unusual-transaction review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundation Law), Law No. 25 of 1995, as amended; incorporating by reference relevant sections of the Panamanian Civil Code; Articles 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 18, 25 and 32 govern formation, endowment, administration, and registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Department)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter) followed by the formal inscription in the Register of Private Interest Foundations; the resulting certificate is the Certificado de Fundación (Foundation Certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Initial foundation capital of at least USD 10,000 must be subscribed; payment may be deferred and made in installments, and no escrow account is required by Panamanian law for a Private Interest Foundation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME], adopted on [DATE]. The undersigned members, being duly designated in the foundation charter, resolve: (1) to accept the founder's endowment of USD 10,000 as initial foundation capital; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Panama City address] as the statutory seat and appoint the licensed law firm named therein as resident agent; (3) to approve the foundation bylaws submitted to this meeting; (4) to appoint [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary of the Foundation Council with joint and several signatory powers; and (5) to instruct counsel to perfect registration of the foundation with the Public Registry and to obtain certified copies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Departamento de Denominaciones (online platform or counter service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official name reservation request in Spanish with three ranked proposed names, each containing the mandatory suffix 'Fundación' or 'Foundation'. Attach the notarized power of attorney of the resident agent. Pay the reservation tariff and collect the issued name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney in favor of resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, resubmit with new proposed names and pay a new tariff; no formal appeal is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública within the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold before a Panamanian notary for execution of the foundation charter and constituent bylaws. The founder or attorney-in-fact declares the foundation's purpose, endowment, foundation council, beneficiaries, and registered office. All documents are notarized in Spanish; if originals are in English, a certified Spanish translation must be attached.
required_dossiers: Draft foundation charter and bylaws in Spanish
Passport copies and notarized powers of attorney for all foundation council members
Proof of registered office address and resident agent acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary qualifies a defect, execute an amendment or re-execute the instrument before the same or another notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized foundation charter and all annexes to the Public Registry, together with the official cover form and registration fee payment. The Registry reviews the legal formalities, the foundation purpose, the endowment statement, the designation of the foundation council, and the resident agent appointment before issuing the foundation certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified Spanish translation of any non-Spanish documents
Resident agent consent and certification of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect or legal objection is notified, deliver a written response with a curing instrument within 10 business days; failing that, file a reconsideration petition with the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Resident Agent Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian law firm or corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and file the registered agent acceptance, acknowledging the fixed address in Panama and the agent's authority to receive judicial and administrative service. The agent issues a certificate of registered office and agent consent for inclusion in the foundation record.
required_dossiers: Letter of acceptance from the resident agent
Lease or letter of address consent from property owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office address is rejected by the agent or the Registry, substitute a compliant address and file a change of registered office notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Fees and Issuance of Foundation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Treasury of the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Settle the official state fee for foundation registration at the Registry's treasury window or through the online collection portal. After payment and Registry approval, obtain the Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Fundación) and certified copies of the inscribed charter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not reflected, present the bank deposit receipt and request treasury reconciliation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Foundation Council and Beneficiary Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder and licensed resident agent before Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the foundation charter names the initial Foundation Council members, the protector (if any), and the beneficiaries in accordance with the founder's asset-management objectives. If any appointment is left to a later instrument, execute and notarize a supplementary foundational deed and file it with the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Beneficiary designation schedule or supplemental deed
Signed acceptance of appointment by each council member
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns a query on beneficiary designation, file an explanatory note and, where necessary, a formal amendment deed signed by the founder and council.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Empresas
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación / Municipal Business Tax License (Patente Municipal) – non-industrial retail permit for online commerce and warehouse logistics

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is online retail and warehousing with no industrial transformation or land alteration; no EIA study or registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharge permits are required; comply with municipal sanitary sewer limits under Panama's wastewater technical standards, Law 41 of 2017 on environmental responsibility, and Law 1 of 2018 on solid waste management; packaging waste must be separated and recycled; no VOC emission thresholds are triggered because no finishing or manufacturing occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain fire safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Inspección Técnica Contra Incendios) for the warehouse; maintain structural load validation for storage racks and floor; secure a favorable Ministry of Labor (MITRADEL) workplace safety inspection where employees handle oversized furniture.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); online portal: SISTEMA E-TAX 2.0 (https://etax.mef.gob.pa). The DGI administers the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC), the ITBMS registry, the mandatory electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) platform, and the taxpayer fiscal mailbox (Buzón Fiscal).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Panamanian Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in online retail, the statutory procedure is: (1) incorporate the PIF before the Public Registry and appoint a resident agent (agente residente) and, where taxable local activity exists, a Panamanian-domiciled fiscal representative; (2) register with the DGI through the E-TAX 2.0 portal by submitting the foundation deed, the resident agent acceptance, a local service address, and a certified copy of the Ficha de Fundación inscribed in the Registro Público; (3) obtain the RUC and the ITBMS registration; (4) obtain a Panamanian digital signature certificate (firma digital) from the accredited certification authority to sign XML invoices; (5) request authorization to issue electronic invoices through the Factura Electrónica module; and (6) where goods are imported into Panama for delivery to Panamanian customers, register as importer of record with the Dirección Nacional de Aduanas (SIGA system). A PIF whose activities are strictly foreign-source is not required to obtain an RUC, but the e-commerce sale of oversized furniture to customers in Panama creates a mandatory registration obligation for the online seller irrespective of local physical presence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: Panama applies a territorial income tax system; a Private Interest Foundation (Law 25 of 1995, as amended) is a hybrid entity. Income derived from sources outside Panama is exempt, and assets held abroad are not subject to Panamanian income tax. However, Panama-source income realized through online retail (sales delivered to customers in Panama) is taxable at the standard corporate rate of 25% on net taxable income, and the PIF remains subject to the annual flat foundation tax of USD 300. The PIF is not automatically tax-exempt when it engages in commercial activity within the Republic of Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a US-style check-the-box classification regime. Law 25 of 1995 permits a PIF, through a formal foundation council resolution, to elect to be governed by the tax provisions applicable to public or private corporations (sociedades anónimas) for the administration of its estate and business. A taxpayer with annual gross turnover not exceeding USD 36,000 may elect the Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente (small taxpayer regime) and adopt simplified ITBMS reporting on a quarterly basis. No hybrid-mismatch election exists under Panamanian law; cross-border planning relies on the objective territorial-source nexus rules, which the DGI applies on a transaction-by-transaction basis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — Panama's national VAT-type consumption tax established by Law 23 of 2016 and regulated by Executive Decree 21 of 2016. The Republic of Panama uses the US Dollar as legal tender; all ITBMS obligations are denominated in USD (Balboa at par).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold is prescribed: any person, including a foreign online seller or a Panamanian PIF, that performs taxable supplies of goods or services which are realized, utilized, or delivered within Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS from the first taxable transaction. The optional Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente applies to annual gross taxable turnover of no more than USD 36,000, permitting quarterly payment and simplified invoicing; non-resident digital and e-commerce sellers of tangible goods to Panama consumers must register and appoint a fiscal representative regardless of turnover under DGI rules governing foreign suppliers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide e-invoicing (Factura Electrónica) is enforced through the SISTEMA E-TAX 2.0 platform. The DGI requires the electronic transmission of XML invoices for real-time validation and clearance at issuance; each invoice receives an acceptance acknowledgement (comprobante de recepción) and must display a QR security code. Taxpayers must transmit the invoice data to the DGI using the Panamanian digital signature, and the invoice number must be pre-authorized by the fiscal administration (rango de facturación). E-commerce sellers of oversized furniture must issue the electronic invoice at checkout for Panamanian customers, transmit the XML to the DGI, and retain the acceptance receipt as a condition for ITBMS credit in the purchaser's name. Imported goods accompanied by the customs declaration (DEX) are cleared through the Dirección Nacional de Aduanas SIGA platform, which is cross-referenced with the DGI fiscal database.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% ITBMS applies to (a) the definitive sale and physical export of movable goods shipped out of Panamanian territory by the seller; (b) services rendered abroad or exclusively to non-resident persons, including international freight, logistics, and fulfilment services that are ancillary to the export of oversized furniture, provided the recipient is located outside Panama and the benefit of the service occurs abroad; and (c) goods introduced into and re-exported from free zones (zonas francas) under customs control. For the Panamanian PIF selling online to foreign customers, the 0% rate is available only where legal title transfers outside Panama and the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory within the period stated in the export declaration; supplies delivered to customers within Panama, including delivery to Panama free-trade-zone permanent establishments, are taxable at 7%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración de Exportación (DEX / Formulario Aduanero Único) validated electronically through the SIGA/SISCO customs system of the Dirección Nacional de Aduanas
Conocimiento de Embarque (Bill of Lading) or Guía Aérea (air waybill) evidencing physical departure of the oversized goods from Panamanian territory
Certificado de Embarque (embarkation certificate) issued by the carrier or shipping agent
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or bank transfer record evidencing settlement of the export proceeds in the exporter's Panamanian banking account
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referenced to the zero-rated fiscal invoice (factura con tarifa 0%) issued through the E-TAX 2.0 platform
Certificate of origin and, if applicable, the free-zone certificate of exit for goods previously admitted to a zona franca
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the Dirección Nacional de Aduanas jointly audit export zero-rating claims through post-clearance reviews that cross-match the export declaration, the bill of lading, the carrier manifest, and the inward remittance certificate held by the exporting bank. Exporters that cannot substantiate the physical export, that overstate export values, or that fail to repatriate hard-currency proceeds within the 180-day period are liable for the ITBMS at 7% on the full invoice value, recalculated retroactively, plus annual interest at 10% (Código Fiscal Article 738-A) and a late-payment surcharge of not less than 10% of the tax due. Issuance of zero-rated invoices without genuine underlying exports constitutes tax and customs fraud, subject to fines of USD 100 to USD 5,000 per infraction, a penalty of up to three times the evaded tax, confiscation of the goods or equivalent value, and criminal prosecution under the tax-fraud provisions of the Código Penal (Article 278-B and money-laundering predicate rules in Law 23 of 2015), which may lead to imprisonment for responsible foundation council members and revocation of the PIF's operating authorization. Claimed input ITBMS credits or refunds linked to fictitious exports are clawed back with retroactive effect within the DGI's five-year limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a central bank with monetary policy or foreign-exchange issuance functions. The financial-system supervisory authority is the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established under Decree Law 9 of 1998, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) manages fiscal policy. The national currency, the Balboa (PAB), is token coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity with the United States dollar, which is legal tender in Panama. There is no independent central-bank exchange-rate mechanism, foreign-exchange reserve management, or central-bank control affecting a Private Interest Foundation's treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Panama maintains a wholly dollarized, current-account and capital-account liberalized regime with no statutory exchange controls, no licensing of foreign-exchange transactions, no profit-remittance approval, and no surrender requirements. The Private Interest Foundation can receive capital injections, online-retail proceeds, BNPL settlements, and intra-group funding in USD or any freely convertible currency without prior central-bank consent. The practical hurdles are compliance-related: the foundation must establish economic substance, maintain books and records, and satisfy Law 23 of 2015 AML/KYC onboarding, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth documentation. Dividends, beneficiary distributions, and profit remittances are not blocked by FX rules, though Panamanian-source income may be subject to territorial taxation and must be declared to the Dirección General de Ingresos.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no central-bank reporting requirement on export receipts. Export proceeds from online retail or marketplace sales in USD, EUR, CNY, or other freely convertible currencies may be retained indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts. The sole administrative obligation is to preserve underlying trade documents, including commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or airway bills, and customs export declarations, to satisfy Law 23 of 2015 anti-money-laundering record-keeping duties for a period of at least five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned commercial bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium (conditional). Panama has no dedicated EU-style electronic-money-institution licence; fintech payment service providers operate under the SBP financial-innovation regime or as licensed banks, and an offshore digital EMI cannot independently access Panama's domestic clearing rails without a sponsoring Panamanian bank. A compliant treasury may use an offshore EMI (for example, a global business account provider) as a payment-collection gateway for Stripe and Affirm BNPL proceeds, provided that the EMI is contractually designated as a payment processor only and that all reserve liquidity is swept daily into the foundation's tier-1 Panamanian bank account. The Panamanian bank remains the SBP-supervised anchor treasury. The PIF must submit a complete KYC packet to the EMI and the sponsoring bank, and any local payment-service arrangement must avoid commingling of platform settlements with foundation capital funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandatory for the remote founder or beneficiary. In market practice, the PIF's designated resident agent, a Panamanian attorney or licensed fiduciary, must physically appear or appear by secure live video to authenticate the foundation deed and sign the account mandate, while the beneficial owner completes an interactive video interview with the bank's compliance officer. Certain tier-1 banks, including Banco General and Banistmo, may request a physical branch visit from the foundation council president or treasurer when projected monthly turnover is high or the online retail model shows repeated chargebacks. Apostilled or legalised corporate certificates, the Certificado de Persona Jurídica from the Registro Público, and source-of-funds statements must be filed in all remote-opening scenarios.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF structure opacity: the foundation charter is private in its detailed beneficial-ownership provisions and the beneficiaries are not publicly registered, which triggers a high-risk classification at the bank's onboarding committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated copy of the Private Interest Foundation deed, notarised and apostilled, with the founding declaration of endowment; a current Foundation Council minute appointing the authorised signatories; a Certificado de Persona Jurídica from the Registro Público; a sworn beneficial-ownership declaration using the SBP-compliant form; and an attorney's legal opinion describing the foundation's economic purpose, the ISIC 4791 online-retail business model, and the source of the endowment funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High online-retail chargeback or BNPL refund pattern associated with oversized furniture (freight damage, delivery delays, customer disputes), which may suggest consumer harm or undisclosed third-party flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and Affirm payout settlement reports, a refund ledger with customer resolution status, the published returns and refund policy, exception reports for oversized-freight damages and delivery delays, logistics exception documents from the last-mile carrier, and a reconciliation of settled amounts against the foundation's operational account entries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large repetitive MT103 wires to third-party suppliers in manufacturing jurisdictions (for example, Vietnam, China, and Eurozone countries) with perceived mismatch between the foundation's declared capital and the payment volume.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and supply agreements, proformas and final commercial invoices, ocean or air waybills with container or tracking identifiers, customs export declarations, freight-forwarder invoices, insurance certificates, and a treasury payment-authorisation matrix demonstrating a four-eyes senior-signatory approval process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hybrid foundation versus active trading company: the account officer questions why a Private Interest Foundation rather than a stock corporation is executing marketplace retail sales, creating a potential economic-substance deficiency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A foundation statute expressly permitting e-commerce and commercial activities, minutes of the Foundation Council authorising the online-retail business, the minimum initial endowment held in the clearing bank, municipal Aviso de Operación registration, RUC tax-registration certificates, platform merchant contracts, and monthly management accounts evidencing real transactions with identifiable customers and suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of aggregated PSP settlement accounts (Stripe/Affirm) that commingle cross-border customer funds, making it difficult to identify the underlying counterparties in a suspicious-transaction review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform-level transaction ledgers with customer names, country codes, order numbers, payment amounts, and currency; PSP merchant agreements; PCI DSS compliance attestations; periodic reconciliation statements matching each settlement batch to the foundation's bank account; and a written funds-flow memorandum describing the payment chain from customer payment to bank credit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing: (1) Founder capital injections arrive by SWIFT MT103 from the founder's verified bank account to the foundation's Capital Escrow Account, with remittance information referencing the foundation deed and the character of the contribution as 'Foundation capital contribution'; Panama applies no exchange-control approval, but the receiving bank must be able to classify the transaction under Law 23 of 2015 and the narrative must not be ambiguous. (2) Retail sales proceeds from Stripe and Affirm BNPL are settled in USD directly to the foundation's Operational Account, either by ACH or SWIFT, and are matched against the PSP's payout statements and order-level transaction reports. (3) Intra-group treasury funding is supported by a written loan agreement, an interest-and-repayment schedule, and board resolutions authorising the borrowing. (4) Verification procedures require the foundation's current juridical-person certificate, council resolutions appointing signatories, and three months of historical platform settlement statements to establish expected transaction velocity. Since Panama has no central-bank statistical purpose-code regime, the SWIFT field 70 narrative must simply state 'Trade settlement' or 'Capital contribution under Panama law' in a clear, non-misleading manner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) For high-value factory purchase orders for oversized furniture, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit is issued via SWIFT MT700, usually confirmed by an international advising bank, with reimbursement through MT103 or MT202 after compliant document presentation (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of quality, and transport evidence). (2) For freight, insurance, port charges, and payments below the LC threshold, the foundation executes SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers directly from its USD operational account through the bank's US correspondent network (CHIPS/Fedwire), embedding the invoice number and purchase-order reference in the payment narrative. (3) Domestic outflows for customs brokerage, port disbursements, and last-mile freight clear through Panama's interbank USD settlement systems; the bank retains the supporting trade documents for the statutory five-year period. No export-surrender or conversion duty applies to any of these outbound disbursements, but the bank must maintain a complete audit trail for each payment chain.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign exchange at the Panamanian bank's treasury desk for immediate USD/EUR or USD/CNY conversion on supplier invoices; the Balboa/USD peg eliminates domestic-currency risk, but third-currency exposure remains and requires transaction-level hedging.

Deliverable FX forward contracts (USD against EUR and offshore CNY) executed with an SBP-licensed bank or its international treasury affiliate, with tenors matched to the foundation's confirmed purchase orders for oversized furniture sourcing.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY or USD where the underlying import invoice is CNY-denominated and onshore deliverability is unavailable; the NDF is executed through the bank's offshore treasury desk and must be supported by a documented underlying commercial exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD or USD/CNH) for procurement financing above USD 500,000, executed under an ISDA/CSA master agreement with the clearing bank; Panama law does not prohibit such instruments, and the swap is structured offshore to avoid Panamanian territorial tax relevance.

Embedded FX hedging through commercial LC currency clauses, denominating the letter of credit in USD while sourcing from EUR or CNY suppliers, allowing the advising bank to provide a fixed conversion quotation at confirmation and serving as a zero-premium hedging discipline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Return (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final) for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: annual confirmation due within 30 days of the foundation's initial UBO filing anniversary; any change in beneficial ownership, control, or foundation council membership must be updated within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Law 129 of 2018 (generally B/.1,001–B/.5,000 per violation); the resident agent is jointly liable; clearance certificates (Paz y Salvo) are withheld while in default, blocking registrations and public deeds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Franquicia) – Flat Government Maintenance Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá), remitted through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable with respect to each current calendar year on or before 31 December; agents customarily require settlement by 30 June to avoid registry delinquency flags
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory default interest (approximately 1% per month) plus late-payment surcharge; after two consecutive unpaid years the foundation is placed on the Registry's delinquency list and becomes subject to administrative strike-off (disolución administrativa) by the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Resident Agent and Registered Office Agreement (Mantenimiento de Agente Residente)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panama Resident Agent (law firm) under Law 25 of 1995; privately contracted, not a government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of the foundation deed's registration date; renewal is invoiced annually, normally during Q1 or Q4
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent results in suspension of registry standing, inability to obtain good-standing certificates, and eventual administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Panama Income Tax Return (Formulario 101) – Applicable only if the PIF derives Panama-source taxable income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March following the close of the prior calendar tax year, or such other date as notified by the DGI for that fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the tax payable plus statutory monthly interest; understatement and willful evasion penalties attach, including criminal liability under the Panamanian Fiscal Code.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación) – Required only if the foundation maintains a physical commercial premises in Panama; municipality-specific tariff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipality (Alcaldía) of the registered business premises, e.g., Alcaldía de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal fixed by municipal ordinance, generally during 1 January – 31 July of the operating year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fines and closure orders for unlicensed commercial activity; unpaid municipal patent fees may accrue surcharges and prevent issuance of municipal good-standing certificates.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory for a Panama Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995, and no public filing of financial statements is required. An independent audit by a Panamanian certified public accountant (Contador Público Autorizado) becomes compulsory only if the foundation conducts Panamanian taxable activity and (i) annual gross receipts exceed approximately USD 1,500,000, (ii) the DGI classifies it as a large taxpayer (Gran Contribuyente), or (iii) a regulator, bank, or counterparty contractually requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama Legal GAAP (PCGA) is the default framework for non-regulated entities; IFRS as issued by the IASB is mandatory for banks, insurance, reinsurance, and securities-market entities. A cross-border e-commerce PIF may voluntarily adopt IFRS for financing or investor reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Law 129 of 2018 and Executive Decree 731 of 2019 require each PIF to identify and file with the DGI Registry of Beneficial Owners the natural persons who are the founder, any foundation council members, beneficiaries designated by name, or other individuals with control. Bearer participation interests are prohibited; all rights are nominative and must be entered into the foundation's records. The licensed resident agent is responsible for filing the initial declaration and any amendments within 30 days, and for performing an annual verification (anniversary-based) confirming that the registered beneficial-ownership data remains accurate. There is no separate government fee for the UBO annual return, but agent compliance fees apply.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Members (Registro de Miembros del Consejo de la Fundación)
Register of Beneficiaries and Ultimate Beneficial Owners
Foundation Protocol and Minute Book (Libro de Actas del Consejo de la Fundación)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 550–1,100 per year (licensed Panamanian law firm, including registered office, resident agent, UBO filing support, franchise tax processing, and regulatory correspondence)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800–4,500 per annual engagement (typical for a small-to-mid-size e-commerce holding entity with no complex consolidation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% of taxable net income on Panama-source income for legal entities (CIR Art. 783-A, effective 1 January 2019).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: A properly structured Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25/1995 is tax-neutral for Panama purposes: no corporate income tax is assessed on foundation assets, capital contributions, distributions to beneficiaries, or income derived from sources outside Panama. Foreign e-commerce revenue is therefore excluded under Panama's territorial scope. Panama-source online retail income is taxed at 25%; no preferential code rate or tax holiday applies to e-commerce retail distribution. Effective rate is 0% for a pure offshore PIF with no Panama-source trading, but any Panama-source commercial activity converts the foundation into a taxable legal entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 111 - Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas; filed electronically through the DGI Sede Electrónica (www.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, no later than 31 March of the following year. For a non-calendar fiscal year-end, within 3 months after the fiscal-year closing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Ingresos brutos de fuente panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from Panama-source commercial activity, including online furniture sales to Panama consumers, local delivery surcharges and assembly fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF with no Panama-source retail activity must enter 0. Foreign-market e-commerce turnover is excluded under territorial taxation and must not be reported in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Informational disclosure of all gross revenue attributable to foreign-source sales and services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all non-Panama income here for audit transparency. Failure to distinguish source may trigger DGI source-recharacterization, so maintain country-by-country customer and delivery records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold allocable to Panama-source sales: furniture wholesale cost, import duties, freight into Panama, and warehouse handling costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate COGS only against Panama-source revenue. If all revenue is foreign-source, enter 0 and keep full third-party cost documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions: marketing, payment-processing fees, storage, depreciation, registered-agent fees, and professional services necessary to generate Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are accepted solely when required for Panama-source income. General PIF administrative costs unrelated to Panama activities are disallowed; transfer pricing adjustments may be imposed if related-party fees are not at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed as Panama-source gross revenue less allocable deductions and unrecovered losses brought forward within the 5-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Box 1 is 0, Box 5 must be 0. A loss is recognized only to the extent the deductions are properly allocable to Panama-source sales; foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Impuesto sobre la renta calculado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% only when Box 5 is positive. If zero, enter 0 and attach the sworn loss schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Retenciones y pagos anticipados acreditables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable Panamanian tax withholdings and advance income tax instalments paid during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama-source withholding certificates (Formulario 106 or bank/retailer certificates) are creditable. Foreign tax withholdings are not creditable against Panama income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Impuesto líquido por pagar o saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due after credits, or refundable balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay through a Panamanian banking institution using the DGI-generated deposit slip; payments from a PIF's foreign bank account are generally not accepted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing carries a fixed fine of B/.100 to B/.1,000 plus statutory monthly surcharge (recargo) on any unpaid tax and monthly interest at the DGI rate. Non-filing after formal notification can trigger a penalty of up to 100% of the omitted tax. Criminal tax evasion adds fines of 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 113 - Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia; submitted through the DGI Sede Electrónica as an annex to the annual income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Concurrent with the Formulario 111 income tax deadline: 31 March after calendar year-end or 3 months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line A - Operaciones con partes relacionadas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate value of related-party transactions, including cross-border purchasing of furniture from affiliated suppliers, group freight contracts, loans, royalties, and management charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PIF transacting with its founder, forbearance council, protector, or companies controlled by them must disclose those transactions in full. Swiss/NGO thresholds do not apply; monetary amounts must be reported in USD/Balboa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line B - Método de precios de transferencia utilizado
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the arm's length method selected for each category of controlled transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the best-fit method among CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM or Profit Split. A summary benchmarking note must be kept for the DGI, even if no adjustment is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line C - Ajuste de precios de transferencia
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Any voluntary or audit-triggered increase in taxable income to align with the arm's length principle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF's foreign-supply chain is economically managed from Panama but invoiced through a related shell, DGI may reattribute income and require a TP adjustment to Panama-source taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Omission or inaccurate TP disclosure is penalized at 1% of the value of the unreported related-party transactions, with a minimum fine of B/.1,000 and maximum of B/.100,000. Failure to maintain contemporaneous documentation triggers additional fines and full recharacterization risk.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% general / 20% exempt-income distributions as stated above
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply reduced withholding under an applicable DTA, the non-resident recipient must submit a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its country of tax residence, apostilled or legalized, together with Formulario 1293 (application for reduced withholding) to the DGI and to the Panamanian withholding agent before the payment date. The Panamanian payer must retain the signed declaration and TRC in its records for 6 years and file the corresponding DGI notification. Panama's DTA network is limited; principal agreements in force and applied in practice include those with Mexico, Spain, South Korea and the United Kingdom. Where no DTA applies, the statutory final withholding rate is conclusive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panama withholding on cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-residents is generally levied at 12.5% of the gross payment; interest from certain qualifying interbank or registered public-debt transactions may be subject to preferential or exempt treatment. Under applicable DTAs, royalties and interest rates may be reduced to up to 10% or 0%, subject to TRC, beneficial ownership test, and prior DGI application. The PIF's online e-commerce platform use of software/IP must document stream of royalties separately from trading profits; intercompany interest must be at arm's length with term sheets and full servicing evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD/Balboa 2,000,000 for Local File and Formulario 113; USD/Balboa 10,000,000 for Master File
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) implemented under Law 254 of 2021 apply to Panamanian-resident legal entities, including PIFs, that carry out 'relevant activities' and earn relevant income from those activities. An online furniture retail and distribution operation managed in Panama qualifies as a Distribution and Service Centre, requiring physical business presence, qualified employees, board supervision, expenditure in Panama proportionate to the activity, and annual ESR filing. A purely passive PIF holding foreign e-commerce investments is only subject to the light reduced-substance requirement and must not hold itself out as exercising commercial activity in Panama. Failure to comply with ESR triggers administrative penalties of USD 10,000 to USD 200,000 per fiscal year and can cause the PIF's registration to be struck off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately routing Panamanian online furniture sales revenues through a foreign shell subtract, then declaring the income as foreign-source, while the PIF's founder, servers, storage, customer support, and commercial decisions remain in Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI recharacterization of the omitted sales as Panama-source income; 25% tax on the recharacterized amount plus 100% penalty on the omitted tax, statutory recargo and interest; criminal tax evasion conviction carries fines of B/.5,000 to B/.100,000 and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, forbearance council members and the resident agent who sign or approve false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and penalties. Courts may order personal asset attachment, travel bans (prohibición de salida), and disqualification from acting as director of any Panamanian entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell PIF / Sham for E-commerce Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PIF as a mere nominee with no board minutes, no transfer-pricing documentation, no beneficial-owner file, no segregated accounting records, and no Panamanian physical substance, while managing the cross-border furniture business from Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registro Público may strike the foundation after repeated non-compliance; ESR penalties between B/.10,000 and B/.200,000 per year; the PIF's contracts and invoicing may be voided as a sham and the underlying economic activity taxed directly to the founder or beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate veil is pierced, the founders and council members are personally liable for the foundation's debts, including tax liabilities. Civil restitution of distributed sums and personal fines of up to B/.250,000 may be imposed; directors may face a 5-year ban from serving in Panama-registered entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing the identity of the founder, protectors or final beneficiaries; issuing or allowing bearer participation certificates where the holder is not disclosed; accepting proceeds from customers through Stripe/Affirm without a Panamanian AML risk assessment; failing to maintain the PIF's UBO register with the resident agent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) fines from B/.1,000 to B/.1,000,000 and suspension of the foundation's operations. Criminal money-laundering charges, if the furniture payments are linked to organized crime, carry prison terms of 5 to 12 years and confiscation of the PIF's assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Councillors and the resident agent are personally subject to criminal indictment if they knowingly facilitate anonymous benefit transfers. Travel bans, passport surrender, pre-trial detention, and personal asset freezing are available under Panama's AML procedural rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold on Distributions of Panama-Source Profits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF earns Panama-source taxable profit from furniture sales but distributes the after-tax surplus to foreign beneficiaries without applying the 10% dividend WHT or the 20% rate for profits not previously taxed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI assesses the full withholding tax on the gross distribution as a primary liability of the PIF, plus a 50% surcharge for failure to withhold, statutory recargo and interest. The beneficiary remains jointly liable for the tax where Panama cannot collect from the foundation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The council member or administrator who authorizes the distribution is jointly and severally liable for the unwithheld amount under the responsible-third-party doctrine. Civil recovery can include bank garnishment, mortgage lien on personal property, and prohibition on leaving Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Pay Annual Foundation Franchise Levy
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The PIF either does not pay the statutory annual franchise fee of B/.300 to the Registro Público, or fails to maintain a registered resident agent and registered office in Panama, while continuing to present itself as an active e-commerce operating entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late payment penalties escalate from 10% of the unreported fee to a B/.300 delinquency penalty; after two uninterrupted years of non-payment the foundation's registration is cancelled and the assets may pass to a Public Registry control until regularization. Striking-off prevents the PIF from suing Stripe, payment processors or freight carriers to recover trapped funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be deemed personally responsible for all contracts signed after the registry suspension date. They are also barred from appearing before the Registro Público, obtaining new corporate formations, and may be personally sued by creditors for fraudulent trading.
